messages:
ashley.k: heads up — ran a wider AWQ act-quant sweep on the new llamaX-13B candidate and hit a weird oscillation in serving. saw spikes in tail latency + quality regression on a small fraction (~0.7%) of requests after ~12h of canary traffic. screenshots + logs here: https://internal/snapshots/2934567 :eyes:

jiwon: can you paste the minimal log snippet? is this during kv warmstart or steady-state?

ashley.k: steady-state. pasted log slice below. looks correlated with group size and a particular batch-size distribution.

ashley.k: ```
[2026-03-18T03:21:11Z] req=0x7fae kv_prefetch group_size=47 batch=8 seq=512 latency=83ms tokens=34
[2026-03-18T03:21:11Z] req=0x7fb2 sample_prob_std=0.28 decode_steps=120
[2026-03-18T03:21:11Z] req=0x7fae fallback_check actq_variance=high
[2026-03-18T03:21:11Z] req=0x7fb2 resp_delay=420ms
```

matt: group_size=47? that's an odd number — we usually see issues when group boundaries aren't aligned with our allocator chunking. did you run with dynamic grouping enabled?

ashley.k: yes, dynamic grouping ON (we were trying to optimize for mixed-length traffic). act quant mode is per-layer per-group. AWQ profile used for canary: awq-v2/auto-act-tune.

luis: quick hypothesis: unaligned group_size + kv prefetch + continuous batching -> mispredicted KV cache offsets -> frequent cache invalidations -> occasional long tail as runtime rebuilds KV segments. that would explain spikes and the 0.7% rate (rare alignment combos).

nora.q: also worth checking numerical drift: some AWQ act quant configs can push activations to border cases and cause higher entropy at decode time (we saw similar with group sizes that split activation quant bins oddly). Did you compare cross-eval perplexity distributions vs GPTQ/INT8/FP8?

ashley.k: yes — quick summary from the bakeoff:
- FP8 baseline: PPL delta +0.0 (reference)
- GPTQ (4-bit tuned): PPL delta +0.6
- INT8 (symmetric): PPL delta +1.8
- AWQ actq (group=32): PPL delta +0.9
- AWQ actq (group=47): PPL delta +2.7 (and heavier tail latencies)

jiwon: interesting. so 47 both hurts quality and correlates with latency. do you have dropout/seed differences? could be a deterministic quantization rounding edge-case.

ashley.k: we re-ran identical seeds, same behavior. reproducible in staging with the same traffic pattern (small fraction of long prefix + many short requests interleaved).

matt: can we reproduce locally with a synthetic workload? try injecting the pattern: random short chats + 1 long prefix every N requests and see if group assignment cycles into the bad alignment. if it reproduces, we can bisect grouping logic.

ashley.k: started a local reproducer job (job id: reproduce-2934). config below:```
./reproducer --model llamaX-13b-awq --group-size 47 --dynamic-group true --kv-prefetch true --pattern "8xshort,1xlong" --seed 42 --rps 150
```

luis: if local repro works, try a quick experiment: 1) force group_size=32 (power-of-two) 2) enable group-jitter (random +/-1) 3) disable kv_prefetch for 1h canary. measure tail p95/p99 and PPL.

nora.q: also add a cross-eval on the same prompt set used for regression detection (the eval suite flagged the delta). we need both PPL and exact-match style checks for safety-critical prompts.

ashley.k: running those now. first pass results: group=32 drops p99 latency by 70% on the bad requests and PPL delta goes back to +0.95 (from +2.7). group-jitter alone reduces frequency of oscillation but doesn't fully recover PPL. disabling kv_prefetch removes latency spikes entirely but increases avg latency by ~6% (expected).

jiwon: sounds like two orthogonal issues: allocator/alignment (group-size) and a correctness edge in AWQ act quant under certain group partitions. we should log and file a model-onboarding bug and block rollout until we have either stable grouping rules or a fallback to GPTQ for problematic requests.

matt: propose a short mitigation rollout plan:
- immediate: restrict canary traffic to group_size in {16,32,64} for 24h; disable dynamic-group on canary nodes
- short-term (48h): instrument a per-request actq-warning metric and auto-fallback policy (if actq_variance > threshold and latency > x -> route to GPTQ variant)
- medium-term (2 weeks): fix quantization packing to align with allocator chunks, add invariant tests that sweep odd group sizes and batch distributions

luis: +1. also add a synthetic test that simulates interleaved short/long prefixes in CI so we catch it before canary.

nora.q: I'll draft the model-onboarding bug: label=awq-actq-stability, priority=high, include PPL diffs, tail-latency histograms, reproducer command, and suggested mitigations.

ashley.k: created issue: https://internal/issue/RED-ML-1283 — added logs and reproducer. scheduling a canary rollback window tomorrow 3pm PT to apply immediate restrictions.

jiwon: one more ask: can we add a small runtime guard that refuses non-power-of-two group sizes unless explicit opt-in? it would prevent future accidental dynamic-group picks that are costly.

matt: runtime guard is doable; I'll open an infra PR to default to power-of-two buckets and expose an opt-in flag with a clear warning. target: PR by EOD tomorrow.

ops-bot: scheduled deploy window: 2026-03-19T15:00Z — canary constraints will be applied to cluster redwood-canary-2.

ashley.k: thanks all. I'll keep posting updates in this thread as reproducer/rollout progress. :thumbsup:
